audit.why: 49.26% over 946 games. Levels 1-3 are a free poke window against a Fury-starved Tryndamere, it contests at 4-5, and from Undying Rage onward it is his lane.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 and the 2+ item stage are both sided Jayce, while whys[4] says Undying Rage 'lets him survive your full Cannon-into-Hammer combo' and 'your level-6 is a non-spike', and whys[6] says 'he out-duels you in any extended fight'.
audit.why: The two stages the text hands to Tryndamere are the two the chart hands to Jayce. Packet reference chart Jayce|Jayce|Jayce|Skill|Tryndamere|Skill|Tryndamere matches the captions.
audit.corrected: win[4], win[6] and the matching phases sides set to Tryndamere.

audit.whatIsWrong: Mocking Shout is described three times as a flat slow on your escape. Riot's text: it decreases surrounding champions' Attack Damage, and 'enemies with their BACKS TURNED to Tryndamere also have their Move Speed reduced'. The slow is conditional on facing away.
audit.why: This is the decisive interaction and it is entirely absent. Turning to face him deletes the slow — the part of his kit that makes his spin stick — while the AD reduction still applies either way. A Jayce who knows this kites out of a commit that otherwise kills him.
audit.corrected: Stated in mid, whys[3] and wants.foe[0].

audit.whatIsWrong: Three fields credit his sustain to 'crit lifesteal'. His actual healing is Bloodlust (Q), a 12s cooldown that consumes Fury to heal, and no Grievous Wounds buy is named anywhere.
audit.why: Lifesteal is an item choice you cannot predict; Bloodlust is guaranteed, on a fixed 12s timer, and scales with the Fury he built off your minions. Anti-heal was flagged missing for this matchup and it is the buy that makes his post-6 trades survivable.
audit.corrected: Bloodlust named and Grievous Wounds called in mid, whys[3] and late.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page says to kill 'when Undying Rage is on cooldown' without saying how long that is.
audit.why: Undying Rage is 120/100/80s, Spinning Slash 12/11/10/9/8s, Bloodlust 12s flat, Mocking Shout 14s flat. The 120s R at rank 1 is a genuine two-minute window.
audit.corrected: 120s R and 12s Bloodlust stated in mid.

edits.before: Through 4-5 it tightens - his Fury and crit chance are ramping, he has Spinning Slash to close and Mocking Shout to slow your escape, and crit lifesteal starts healing the poke you land, so keep your distance and use the Hextech Capacitor speed off each stance-swap to kite his spin rather than sit in it. Level 6 is where he takes the wheel: Undying Rage lets him ride your Cannon-Q into Hammer To-the-Skies / Lightning Field / Thundering Blow combo at 1 HP and spin out alive, so do NOT all-in into an up R expecting a kill. Save Thundering Blow to knock him out of spin range when he commits, and only go for the kill when Undying Rage is on cooldown.
edits.after: Through 4-5 it tightens - his Fury and crit chance are ramping, he has Spinning Slash to close and Mocking Shout to slow you. Read that W properly: it only slows enemies with their BACKS TURNED, so facing him removes the slow entirely while it still cuts his AD. And his heal is Bloodlust, a 12s Fury dump, not lifesteal - Grievous Wounds blunts it. Level 6 is where he takes the wheel: Undying Rage rides your Cannon-Q into Hammer To-the-Skies / Lightning Field / Thundering Blow combo out at 1 HP, so do NOT all-in into an up R. Save Thundering Blow to knock him out of spin range, and go for the kill only on the 120s R cooldown.

edits.before: He gets Spinning Slash, Mocking Shout's slow and crit lifesteal to close and heal the poke, so the chip war stops being one-sided - it's genuinely contested.
edits.after: He gets Spinning Slash to close and Bloodlust to heal the poke off Fury; Mocking Shout only slows a turned back, so face him and it is just an AD cut.

edits.before: Build Fury off minions, then Spinning-Slash onto your step-ups and Mocking Shout to slow you inside spin range
edits.after: Build Fury off minions, then Spinning-Slash your step-ups and Mocking Shout as you turn to run - the slow needs your back

edits.before: This is his game, not yours - extended duels are exactly what a crit Tryndamere wants against a defenseless caster. Two items deep he Spinning-Slashes onto your squishy frame, crit-shreds you with lifesteal, and Undying Rage simply negates the burst you'd need to delete him. Keep poking on side waves with gate-Q from max range and use Thundering Blow to shove him off when he dives, but the real plan was banked earlier: convert your level 1-3 lead into plates, kills and an objective so the game ends before his crit and Undying Rage make your poke irrelevant.
edits.after: This is his game, not yours - extended duels are exactly what a crit Tryndamere wants against a defenseless caster. Two items deep he Spinning-Slashes onto your squishy frame, crit-shreds you while a 12s Bloodlust dumps Fury back into health, and Undying Rage negates the burst you'd need to delete him. Executioner's is not optional. Keep poking side waves with gate-Q from max range and Thundering Blow him off when he dives, but the real plan was banked earlier: convert your level 1-3 lead into plates, kills and an objective before his crit scaling makes your poke irrelevant.

notes: Mocking Shout's slow only applies to enemies whose backs are turned — three fields treated it as an unconditional slow, and knowing the condition is what lets you kite his spin. His heal is Bloodlust (12s, consumes Fury), not lifesteal. spikes[1] states Undying Rage lasts 5 seconds; that duration is not in Riot's text and I could not verify it from the kit file, so I left the sentence untouched rather than restate or remove it — recorded as unverified.
